channel: epbs/_threads/and also catching up on the _missing
searchText: I think the proof can, and should, be against the blockhash that fullfiled it Rather than the beacon block that deducted it There are a few options besides the state, we should really go over all possible scenarios, but blockhashes are referenced in bids from very different blocks so one could use in principle very different blocks from the chain of missing ones to prove against a particular blockhash So for example, the case that worries <@808969530608451584>. CL N deducts withdrawals. EL N fullfills them, CL N+1 deducts some more. EL N+1 is missing. CL N+2 doesn't deduct anything, EL N+2 comes and blockroot is CL N+1, not CL N. Client wants to prove the withdrawals that were deducted in N and were fullfilled in the same N, but there's no blockroot for N. Proving via the state seems to add 22 hashes, but proving via the parent root of N+1 only adds a couple as far as I can tell. That is, you provide the blockroot of N and prove that it's the parent root of N+1, then you prove as usual for N. This seems to be cheaper than going through the state.
